These Appeals, Coming On For Final Hearing, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice E.S.Indiresh
 Oral Judgment

1. In these appeals, the appellant-Corporation has assailing the Judgment and award dated 24.06.2019 passed in MVC No.1288/2015, MVC No.1289/2015 and MVC No.1290/2015 on the file of the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VII, Vijayapura (for short 'the Tribunal') awarding compensation to the respective claimants.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:1093 HC-KAR 2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The facts in nutshell for the purpose of adjudication of these appeals are that, the claimants were travelling in APE Auto rickshaw bearing registration No.MH- 23/X-1244 towards Solapur from Kumbari side, and at that time, a bus bearing registration No.KA-32/F-1735 which came from opposite side was driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the said auto rickshaw and as a result the claimants sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, the claimants have preferred the claim petition before the Tribunal, seeking compensation.

sentences.text: After service of notice, the respondent- Corporation has entered appearance and filed detailed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. The Tribunal after considering the material on record, by its Judgment and award dated 24.06.2019 awarded compensation of Rs.2,40,225/- in MVC NC: 2026:KHC-K:1093 HC-KAR No.1288/2015, Rs.25,000/- in MVC No.1289/2015 and Rs.99,000/- in MVC No.1290/2015 with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved the same, the respondent- corporation preferred these appeals.

6. Heard Sri. Sharnabasappa M. Patil, learned counsel for the appellant-corporation and Sri.
Sanganagouda V. Biradar lerned counsel appearing for the respondents- claimants.
7.

Sri. Sharanabasappa M. Patil, learned counsel appearing for the appellant contended that the Tribunal has failed to consider the fact that, the auto rickshaw was plying on the road by exceeding the seating capacity of the passengers and as such, the driver of the auto rickshaw lost control and the said aspect was ignored by the Tribunal and accordingly sought for interference of this Court.
8. Per contra, Sri. Sanganagouda V. Biradar, learned counsel appearing for the claimants sought to justify the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:1093 HC-KAR 9.

Having taken note of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties,
particularly as to the Issue No.1 answered by the Tribunal, wherein, though the respondent-corporation has examined the driver of the bus in question, however, failed to prove the negligence on the part of the driver of the auto rickshaw.
It is also to be noted that as per the police records, the charge-sheet has been filed against the driver of the bus.

In that view of the matter,
taking into account the finding recorded by the tribunal on Issue No.1, I am of the view that, no interference is called for with regard to the liability.

10. Insofar as the award of compensation is concerned, having taken note of the finding recorded by the Tribunal as well as the injuries sustained by the claimants in the said accident, I am of the view that, no interference is called for.
